newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS TO STAY AT DELLE ALPI STADIUM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS TO STAY AT DELLE ALPI STADIUM.

text.p: Serie A leaders Juventus look set to stay at the unpopular Delle Alpi stadium they share in Turin next season after a financial deal with the local council, the Italian sports newspaper Tuttosport said on Wednesday.

Tuttosport said a plan to increase sponsorship revenue from matches at the Delle Alpi meant that Juventus, who will defend their European Cup title against Borussia Dortmund later this month, were unlikely to go through with threats to move.
"It could be that the prospect of larger earnings has softened the position of the club's management," Tuttosport said. No-one at the club was available for comment.
Juventus, as well as fellow tenants Torino, have complained for years about the costs of playing at the futuristic Delle Alpi stadium and in 1995 Juve played a UEFA Cup semifinal in Milan in protest.
This season, Juventus played their European Supercup final against Paris St Germain in Palermo, Sicily.
However, in spite of the extension to the current arrangement, both clubs are still planning to move away in the longer term.

Tuttosport said Juventus hoped to return to their old Comunale stadium by 2000 while Torino, who were relegated from serie A last season, want to return to the Filadelfia stadium for the first time since 1966.
